producer_report.summary:
I made the firstmate page define each term once and link to it everywhere else. I tested the new link handling and ran the xtask, policy and cap-study tests; they pass. For fmt, clippy and the workspace test I ran only the cargo commands, listed below, and the recorded runs are left to Athena.

- **Link markup:** `[[term]]` in intro text now renders as `<a href="#term-slug">` through a new `linked()` helper in `xtask/src/site.rs`.
- **Words used first:** it now holds the one definition of captain, yolo, in scope, green and red, and each of those entries has an anchor id. I removed their duplicate Glossary entries and the duplicate home entry from Words used first.
- **Glossary:** it keeps home, place and places-held. I dropped the sentence about when a place is freed from the places-held entry, since the place entry already says it.
- **Links elsewhere:** the overview, walkthrough, t3/t4/t10 summaries, failure list and counters lead-in now link to those definitions instead of restating them.
- **Tests:** a new test checks that the Glossary or Words used first holds exactly one definition each of yolo, green, red, in scope, place, places-held and home. It checks that none of their definition sentences repeats on the rendered page, that ids are unique, and that every term link has a matching id. A small second test covers the link markup. Three existing tests changed to expect the single definition.
- **Changelog:** I added an entry.

I ran `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p xtask`, `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` and `cargo test -p athena-cap-study`. All passed.

I reworded some sentences but kept their original claim citations, and I did not re-read the claim text for each one. That is the one thing a reviewer should check.

checks_run.note: 83 unit tests plus ci_shards, fingerprint, policy, site_page, spec, walltime integration tests all passed

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p xtask`. A new test in xtask/src/site.rs renders the real study and splits the page text into sentences. It asserts that no definition sentence for yolo, green, red, in scope, places or home appears more than once, and it passes.
criteria_check.evidence: New test each_term_is_defined_once_and_every_term_link_resolves in xtask/src/site.rs renders the real study and strips tags and citation lists. It splits each term's definition into sentences and asserts every sentence occurs exactly once on the page. `cargo test -p xtask` passed.

criteria_check.criterion: The same test, or a sibling in xtask/src/site.rs, asserts that each of the terms yolo, green, red, in scope, places and home has exactly one definition on the page. It also asserts that every link to a term (href="#term-...") has a matching id on the page.
criteria_check.evidence: The same test asserts that `<dt id="term-X">X</dt><dd>` occurs exactly once for yolo, green, red, in-scope, place, places-held and home. It asserts ids are unique and that every href="#term-.." has a matching id, with more than 10 links. A second test, a_term_marked_in_double_brackets_becomes_a_link, checks the link markup. Both pass.

criteria_check.criterion: `git diff` shows that studies/firstmate-work-handling/intro.json (and any site.rs template text) no longer restates the definitions in the overview 'what' list, the walkthrough steps, the t4 and t10 summaries or the limits (failure) list. Those places link to the term instead, for example 'yolo' becomes a link to its definition.
criteria_check.evidence: In intro.json the what, walkthrough, limits, t3, t4 and t10 texts, the counters lead-in and the yolo and red limit sentences now use [[yolo]], [[green]], [[red]], [[in scope]], [[place]], [[places-held]] and [[home]] instead of the definition wording. site.rs renders [[x]] as <a href="#term-x">.

criteria_check.criterion: The Glossary and 'Words used first' sections still contain the definitions, with their claim citations kept. The rendered page still cites claims for every factual statement, so the existing citation tests pass.
criteria_check.evidence: Words used first now holds the single definition of captain, yolo, in scope, green and red, each with its citations; the yolo entry also cites c28. The Glossary holds place, places-held and home. The duplicate glossary entries were removed. The existing citation tests pass.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test`. All pass, including the existing site.rs tests and the athena-cap-study study validation tests. Any existing test changed carries a diff showing that it now expects the single definition.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks for the recorded fmt, clippy and workspace test runs. I ran `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` (clean), `cargo test -p xtask` and `cargo test -p athena-cap-study`, all passing. Three existing tests changed in site.rs: the in-scope test (renamed, now expects one definition in Words used first), the start-here term test (now expects `<dt id=...>`) and the glossary-sort test (now expects green, red, yolo, in scope and captain absent from the Glossary). The glossary_terms helper now reads only the Glossary section.

criteria_check.criterion: No unrelated behavior changes. The diff touches only xtask/src/site.rs and the study's intro.json (and CHANGELOG.md if the repository's convention requires an entry); the build output path, evidence section and claims listing are unchanged.
criteria_check.evidence: git status shows only CHANGELOG.md, studies/firstmate-work-handling/intro.json and xtask/src/site.rs modified. Output-path, evidence and claims code were not touched.

open_issues: Statements in intro.json that I reworded keep their original claim citations. I did not re-read the claim text in claims.json for each reworded sentence.
The `place`/`places-held` split: only one of them mentions that a recorded PR or cleanup frees a place. The 'places' definition is split across the two entries by design.
mistakes: My first edit left a trailing comma in start_terms after I removed the home entry; I fixed it before running any test.
learnings: Start-here term dt elements now carry id="term-<slug>", so any test that scans for glossary ids must slice from the Glossary heading.
The producer shell hook allows only cargo, chmod, git, ls, mv and rm; pipes into grep, tail and rg are denied.
